events.title: Early Human Settlement
events.description: Archaeological evidence shows human activity on Timor Island dating back 40,000 years. Early inhabitants likely came from Southeast Asia and Australia.

events.title: Cave Culture
events.description: Multiple prehistoric cave sites discovered on Timor Island, including cave paintings and tools. This proves early humans lived here for tens of thousands of years.

events.title: Austronesian Migration
events.description: Austronesian peoples migrated to Timor Island, bringing agriculture and Neolithic culture. They are ancestors of modern East Timorese.

events.title: Trade Links with Java
events.description: Timor established trade relations with Java's Majapahit Kingdom. Timor exported sandalwood, honey and beeswax.

events.title: Sandalwood Trade Rises
events.description: Timor Island became famous for sandalwood, attracting merchants from China, Java, Malay and other regions. Timor became part of Southeast Asian trade network.

events.title: Traditional Kingdoms Period
events.description: Timor Island had multiple small kingdoms (Liurai, Wehali, etc.) ruled by traditional kings. These kingdoms were foundation of East Timor's traditional society.

events.title: East Timor Unilaterally Declares Independence
events.description: FRETILIN unilaterally declared East Timor's independence, establishing the 'Democratic Republic of East Timor.' However, it was recognized by only a few countries.

events.title: Indonesian Invasion of East Timor
events.description: Indonesian forces massively invaded East Timor (Operation Lotus). Indonesian President Suharto, citing anti-communism, received tacit approval from the US and Australia.

events.title: Indonesian Occupation and Resistance
events.description: Indonesian forces brutally suppressed East Timorese resistance. During 24 years of occupation, about 100,000-180,000 East Timorese (1/4 of the population) died from massacres, famine, and disease. This was one of the 20th century's worst genocides.

events.title: Dili Becomes Portuguese Capital
events.description: Portugal moved East Timor's capital from Oecusse to Dili. Dili became political center of Portuguese Timor.

events.title: Independence Referendum
events.description: Under UN supervision, East Timor held an independence referendum. 78.5% of voters supported independence. This was a historic moment for East Timor.

events.title: East Timor Officially Independent
events.description: East Timor officially became independent, becoming the 21st century's first new independent nation. Xanana Gusmão became first President. May 20 became East Timor's Independence Day.

events.title: Manufahi Rebellion
events.description: Liurai (traditional king) Dom Boaventura led largest rebellion against Portuguese rule. Portugal brutally suppressed it, killing thousands. This strengthened Portuguese colonial control.

events.title: Joins United Nations
events.description: East Timor joined the United Nations, becoming the 191st member state. This marked East Timor's full recognition by the international community.

events.title: Japanese Occupation
events.description: Japan invaded and occupied East Timor during Pacific War. Tens of thousands of Timorese died from Japanese brutality, forced labor and famine. Australia fought guerrilla warfare in Timor.

events.title: Decolonization Movements
events.description: Global decolonization wave influenced East Timor. Timorese students and intellectuals began demanding independence or autonomy. But Portugal ignored these demands.

events.title: Portugal's Carnation Revolution
events.description: Portugal's Carnation Revolution overthrew dictatorship, new democratic government decided to decolonize. East Timor suddenly faced self-determination choice.

events.title: Political Parties Emerge
events.description: Three main parties formed: FRETILIN (independence), UDT (autonomy with Portugal), APODETI (integration with Indonesia). Political divisions emerged.

events.title: Civil War
events.description: UDT staged coup attempting to preempt FRETILIN, triggering civil war. FRETILIN won, controlling most of East Timor. Portugal withdrew, abandoning colony.

events.title: Early Human Habitation
events.description: Archaeological evidence shows humans inhabited Timor Island during the Paleolithic period. Ancient people engaged in hunting, gathering, and fishing.

events.title: Indonesian Occupation
events.description: Indonesia occupied East Timor for 24 years, making it '27th province'. Indonesian military committed systematic atrocities. International community largely ignored East Timor's suffering.

events.title: Genocide and Resistance
events.description: Indonesian military killed 100,000-180,000 East Timorese (1/4 of population) through massacres, forced starvation, disease. FALINTIL guerrillas waged 24-year resistance in mountains.

events.title: Santa Cruz Massacre
events.description: Indonesian military massacred at least 250 peaceful protesters at Santa Cruz cemetery in Dili. Western journalist filmed massacre, shocking world. This became turning point for East Timor's international attention.

events.title: Nobel Peace Prize
events.description: East Timorese Bishop Carlos Belo and resistance leader José Ramos-Horta won Nobel Peace Prize, raising global awareness of East Timor's plight and legitimizing independence movement.

events.title: Suharto Falls
events.description: Indonesia's Suharto dictatorship collapsed. New President Habibie surprisingly offered East Timor referendum choice (autonomy or independence). This opened door to independence.

events.title: Terror Campaign
events.description: Before referendum, Indonesian military and pro-integration militias launched terror campaign, killing hundreds, intimidating voters. International observers witnessed widespread violence.

events.title: Sandalwood Trade
events.description: Timor became an important sandalwood trading center, trading with China, India, and Arab merchants. Sandalwood was valuable export commodity.

events.title: Portuguese Arrival
events.description: Portuguese traders first reached Timor, beginning European influence on the island. Portugal established trading posts for sandalwood and spices.

events.title: Dutch Arrive in West Timor
events.description: Dutch began occupying western Timor, competing with Portugal. Timor Island split into Portuguese (east) and Dutch (west) spheres of influence.

events.title: Dili Becomes Capital
events.description: Portuguese established Dili as East Timor's capital. Dili gradually became political and economic center.

events.title: Treaty of Lisbon
events.description: Portugal and Netherlands signed Treaty of Lisbon, dividing Timor Island. East Timor became Portuguese colony, West Timor Dutch.

events.title: East Timorese Rebellion
events.description: East Timorese launched rebellion against Portuguese rule, but it was suppressed. Portugal strengthened control over East Timor.

events.title: Portuguese Reoccupation
events.description: After Japan's surrender, Portugal regained control of East Timor. But East Timor's economy and society were severely damaged by war.

events.title: Portuguese Carnation Revolution
events.description: Portuguese military coup overthrew dictatorship. New government decided to decolonize, including East Timor. This opened path to East Timor independence.

events.title: East Timor Civil War
events.description: After Portugal withdrew, East Timor's political factions fought civil war. FRETILIN (left-wing) fought UDT (conservative) and APODETI (pro-Indonesia).

events.title: Indonesia Annexes East Timor
events.description: Indonesia formally annexed East Timor as its 27th province. International community mostly didn't recognize the annexation, but provided little practical support.

events.title: Santa Cruz Massacre
events.description: Indonesian forces opened fire on peaceful East Timorese demonstrators at Santa Cruz Cemetery in Dili, killing hundreds. Massacre exposed to world via video, raising international attention to East Timor issue.

events.title: Suharto Falls
events.description: Indonesian President Suharto resigned amid financial crisis and social unrest. New President Habibie showed willingness to resolve East Timor issue.

events.title: Post-Referendum Violence
events.description: After independence referendum, pro-Indonesian militias supported by Indonesian military launched massive revenge violence. 70% of East Timor's infrastructure destroyed, hundreds of thousands displaced.

events.title: UN Transitional Administration
events.description: UN Transitional Administration in East Timor (UNTAET) governed East Timor, restoring order, rebuilding infrastructure, preparing for independence.

events.title: Political Crisis and Violence
events.description: East Timor erupted in political crisis and factional violence, military split. Australian-led international peacekeeping force again deployed to maintain order.

events.title: President Attacked
events.description: President Ramos-Horta seriously injured in rebel attack. This highlighted East Timor's political and security fragility.

events.title: UN Peacekeeping Mission Ends
events.description: UN peacekeeping forces withdrew from East Timor, marking East Timor's entry into new phase of independence and autonomy.

events.title: Oil and Gas Revenue
events.description: East Timor developed Timor Sea oil and gas resources, establishing petroleum fund. Oil revenue became main source of state finances, but also faces resource curse risk.

events.title: Maritime Boundary Agreement with Australia
events.description: East Timor signed Timor Sea Maritime Boundary Treaty with Australia, resolving long-disputed marine resource allocation. East Timor gained more oil and gas revenue.

events.title: Economic Development Challenges
events.description: East Timor remains one of Asia's poorest countries, facing high unemployment, poverty, poor infrastructure. Over-dependent on oil revenue, economic diversification difficult.

events.title: Tasi Mane Project
events.description: East Timor launched ambitious Tasi Mane Project (Greater Sunrise Project), planning to build oil refinery, LNG plant, and supply base. Project controversial, requiring huge investment.

events.title: José Ramos-Horta Re-elected President
events.description: Nobel laureate José Ramos-Horta re-elected President after 10 years. He vowed to fight corruption and promote economic development.

events.title: ASEAN Membership Application
events.description: East Timor continues pushing for ASEAN membership, having applied since 2011. ASEAN membership would help East Timor integrate into regional economy.

events.title: Continued Nation-Building
events.description: Over 20 years independent, East Timor still on difficult nation-building journey. Young population (60% under 25), but limited job opportunities. Political leaders committed to building stable, prosperous nation.

events.title: 經濟發展挑戰
events.description: 東帝汶仍是亞洲最貧窮國家之一，面臨高失業率、貧困、基礎設施落後等挑戰。過度依賴石油收入，經濟多元化困難。...

events.title: 持續建國之路
events.description: 東帝汶獨立20多年，仍在建國之路上艱難前行。年輕人口眾多（60%人口25歲以下），但就業機會有限。政治領袖致力於建設穩定繁榮的國家。...
